title: Dota2 Senate
summary: In the Dota2 game, the Senate, made up of senators from the Radiant ('R') and Dire ('D') parties, votes on a game change through a series of rounds.
statement: In the Dota2 game, the Senate, made up of senators from the Radiant ('R') and Dire ('D') parties, votes on a game change through a series of rounds. Each senator can either ban another senator's voting rights or declare victory if all remaining senators are from the same party. The voting process follows a fixed order and continues until one party wins. Predict the winning party based on the initial composition of the Senate.
constraints: 1 <= len(senate) <= 10,000; every character is R or D.
Senators act cyclically in input order and each active senator bans one opponent.
hints: Relative turn order determines which party receives each ban.
Queue the future turn indices of both parties.
Pop one from each queue; the earlier index survives and returns with index+n.
Pairing the earliest active senators models one ban while preserving the cyclic order of every survivor.
editorial: Pairing the earliest active senators models one ban while preserving the cyclic order of every survivor.

tests.explanation: Radiant acts first and bans the Dire senator.
After Radiant bans one Dire senator, the remaining Dire senator bans Radiant.
